explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/456: p_n is the smallest prime ≡ 1 (mod n), m_n the smallest integer with n | φ(m_n); 'Is it true that m_n < p_n for almost all n?' In Lean p n = sInf{k prime, k ≡ 1 [MOD n]} and m n = sInf{k > 0, n ∣ φ(k)}, both genuine minima for n ≥ 1 (Dirichlet), with only the junk index n = 0 affected. The statement says #{n < N : m_n < p_n}/N → 1, i.e. the set has natural density 1, the standard reading of 'almost all n'. Faithful.
